say: Toilet gel, glass spray and disinfectant: three hazards handled.
This is the video for module 3: Specialist Products.
These three products each carry a specific hazard. The toilet gel is an acid.

say: The ring in a toilet is mostly mineral scale from hard water and urine.
It needs an acid plus time.
Many shop cleaners use hydrochloric acid, spirit of salt.
It is fast, but it gives off corrosive fumes, burns skin badly and eats metal fittings.

panel.heading: Why citric acid, not hydrochloric
right: Easier to handle in a workshop

say: This course uses citric acid.
It works more slowly, so a thick gel clings to the bowl, and your directions give it time: leave for at least 10 minutes, or overnight for heavy scale, then brush and flush.

panel.heading: Why citric acid, not hydrochloric
right: Easier to handle in a workshop

say: Goggles and gloves on, because citric acid dust stings the eyes.

say: Rest it overnight and record the pH. Every toilet cleaner label must warn: do not use with bleach, because acid plus bleach releases chlorine gas, and toilets are small closed rooms.

say: Streaks come from too much surfactant, minerals in the water, and slow drying. So glass cleaner uses very little SLES.

panel.heading: A streak-free spray without ammonia
items: No flames, no smoking, window open

say: Use distilled or deionised water. Test it by letting a few drops dry on a mirror. Good water leaves no ring.

panel.heading: A streak-free spray without ammonia
items: No flames, no smoking, window open

say: Add the isopropyl alcohol last, pouring slowly, and close its container immediately. It makes the spray dry fast.

say: Its vapour can catch fire from a flame some distance away. Switch off any stove or generator nearby, and keep a fire extinguisher by the door.

say: For example, Adaeze in Enugu buys BKC 50%. Her supplier's technical sheet gives 0.2% active BKC for hard surfaces, with a 10-minute contact time. Do not take these figures from social media.

panel.rule: Use the level and contact time from your own supplier's sheet.

say: Dirt shields germs, so directions start with: clean first. The surface must stay wet for the full contact time. Spraying and wiping dry at once does not work.
And keep BKC away from dish liquid. In a jar test, the mix turns cloudy, and that BKC can no longer kill germs.

panel.heading: What your disinfectant label says
left: Leave wet for the contact time
right: Use on skin, wounds or food

say: Never print a germ-kill percentage unless your product has been tested for it.
Never suggest it protects people from disease.
And speak to your NAFDAC state office before selling anything called a disinfectant.

panel.heading: What your disinfectant label says
left: Leave wet for the contact time
right: Use on skin, wounds or food

say: To remember.
Acid plus time removes scale.
Citric acid is far safer.
Glass cleaner needs little surfactant and soft water.
Keep alcohol away from flames.
And for disinfectant, follow your supplier's sheet, pair BKC only with nonionics, and make only honest claims.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Toilet scale needs acid plus contact time
Citric acid is far safer than hydrochloric
Glass: little surfactant, soft water, no ammonia
IPA is highly flammable: no flames
BKC: supplier's level, nonionics only, no hype
